messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: INCIDENT 1957348210 — Elevated latency and 5xx in ap-east-1 impacting Hosted API and Dedicated pools. Symptoms: increased p95 latency, ~15% 5xx for text generation routes and Dedicated model serving errors. Initial signal: AWS control-plane auth timeouts (STS) and increased API call latencies. Paging oncall @alex @maya — please triage and escalate if necessary.

alex: Ack, joining bridge. Starting live triage now.

maya: Ack. Graphs look nasty — p50 ~220ms -> 400ms, p95 spikes to 2.6s, error-rate up starting ~08:08Z. Hosted API and several Dedicated pools in ap-east-1 show matching spike.

samir: Looking at service logs for dedicated agent pool nodes. Seeing repeated token fetch errors to STS and some control-plane 502s.

samir: log snippet:
```
2026-03-15T08:09:58Z | dedicated-agent-42 | WARN | token refresh failed: context deadline exceeded (STS:GetCallerIdentity)
2026-03-15T08:10:12Z | model-server | ERROR | request failed 502: upstream auth timeout
```

june: That matches an AWS advisory I'm watching — elevated STS latencies in ap-east-1. Could be causing our auth to fail for Dedicated instance metadata/service calls. Also might affect ELB health checks.

alex: Quick mitigations in flight: 1) enable region-fallback routing for Hosted API to ap-northeast-1 for compatible models 2) drain new sessions on ap-east-1 dedicated pools 3) increase token cache TTL for existing workers to reduce STS chatter. Doing 1 now.

ops-bot: Executing routing policy change: `rbxctl route apply --policy region-fallback --region ap-east-1 --fallback ap-northeast-1 --models "gpt-*-token"`

alex: Routing change applied, traffic shifted ~30% over 10m. Watching error-rate and latency.

maya: Noted some customers hitting Dedicated pools with pinned allocations — those won't failover automatically. Need to contact CS for impacted customers and consider emergency capacity in other regions.

ben: Filing initial customer-impact ticket and posting to status page. Draft status update: "We are investigating elevated error rates in ap-east-1 impacting API requests and dedicated capacity; mitigation in progress; next update in 15 minutes."

status-bot: Status page incident created: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/1957348210 — incident posted to public page (minor/major TBD).

samir: Temporary hotfix applied: bumped token cache TTL in the runtime to 30m and added jitter to refresh to avoid stampeding. Patch rolled to canaries in ap-east-1.

ops-bot: Canary rollout: 5/5 canaries healthy after token-cache patch. Rolling to 25% of nodes.

maya: Observability note: our metrics ingestion (third-party) is also degraded — some alerting delays ~2min. Correlating data is slower. We're relying on internal metrics for now.

alex: Customer-impact assessment: ~12 customers on dedicated pools in ap-east-1 saw elevated errors; ~5 customers with heavy Hosted API usage experienced increased latencies and intermittent 5xx. No data exfiltration.

ben: CS outreach started for the 12 dedicated customers. Templates ready.

june: Handing off to night oncall (june) in 25m. Leaving runbook notes: - routing fallback enabled - token-cache TTL increased - canary rollout in progress - status page updated - CS engaged. Please escalate to infra lead if errors don't reduce to <2% in next 30m.

alex: Leaving bridge in 10. Handoff ack to @june. Followups: add STS token caching by default for dedicated agents, add fallback triggers when control-plane RT exceeds 500ms, and evaluate cross-region capacity automation.

june: Ack taking over. Will keep watching and coordinate with infra to spin emergency capacity in ap-northeast-1 if needed.

samir: For postmortem: need timeline of third-party (AWS STS) errors, our token refresh pattern, and why pinned dedicated allocations didn't failover gracefully. Recommend action items: conservative token TTL, exponential backoff + jitter for STS calls, route-failover slack runbook, and runbook automation to notify CS earlier.

ben: Drafting post-incident customer communication and internal incident review invite.

incident-bot: Incident 1957348210 — next update scheduled in 15m. :timer_clock:
